title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 — Section 23 (Statements of claim and defence)

content.overview: Within the period agreed by the parties or determined by the tribunal, the claimant states facts supporting the claim, points at issue and relief sought; the respondent states the defence. Parties may submit documents or refer to evidence. Claims or defences may be amended or supplemented unless the tribunal considers it inappropriate having regard to delay.
content.glance: Claim and defence statements within agreed/tribunal timelines; amendments allowed unless inappropriate due to delay.
content.study: The claim must state supporting facts, issues and relief; the defence responds. Documents and evidence may be submitted or referred to. Amendments are permitted during proceedings unless inappropriate having regard to delay.

sections.heading: Claim and defence
sections.body: Claimant states facts, issues and relief; respondent states the defence, within the agreed or determined period.

sections.heading: Documents and evidence
sections.body: Parties may submit relevant documents or refer to evidence to be submitted.

sections.heading: Amendments
sections.body: Claims or defences may be amended or supplemented unless the tribunal considers it inappropriate having regard to delay.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What must a statement of claim contain under section 23?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Facts supporting the claim, the points at issue and the relief or remedy sought.

examTips: State claim contents, defence, and amendment/delay test.

enhancement.definition: Section 23 governs statements of claim and defence and amendments.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Claim and defence within agreed/tribunal timelines; amendments unless inappropriate due to delay.

tenMark.point: State the contents of the defence
tenMark.application: The respondent states the defence in respect of the claim.
Parties may submit documents or add a reference to the evidence they will submit.
Amendments are allowed during proceedings unless the tribunal finds them inappropriate having regard to delay.
